Additional comments

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Hard

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Stay away from M&N accomodation, very shady and uncormfortable to deal with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Living on campus was extremely expensive and poorly maintained

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had to change course after arrivel since I was able to register for a course that later was moved in scheduling.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register for courses before hand. Important to note: as a master student you can only apply for exchange using master courses but once you arrive you can change them out if you so desire.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Introduction days had people helping you out but the system itself was quite flawed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 3/4 and ended up having to pick a physics course I did not have the prereqs for. This happened due to the very limited amount of physics courses offered. And as mentioned there was a problem were I no longer could take one of the courses I wanted from researching.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you have 6-8 courses you would want to take such that if anything happens you have backups

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most were very compareable with uni at KU but one had me failing in spite of me spending more than double the amount of time on it I would at home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most lectures were compareable but some had lectures with people sitting in groups talking while the lecture was ongoing.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Neural networks and deeplearning, Advanced fluid dynamics, Climate models what are they used for, and Characterization of advanced materials.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Neural networks and deeplearning was insightful

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Take the shuttlebus. Be proactive in finding housing, including reaching out to other exchange students. Make time for travel.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make an australian bank account or you can't get your deposit back.
